articles.title: Saudi-Backed Forces Pull Back From Bab el-Mandeb Strait As Houthis Advance Towards Aden
articles.description: Reported by: Wesley Dockery The Southern Armed Forces group allied with Yemen's UN-recognized government and backed by Saudi Arabia said Sunday they had repositioned themselves away from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Why are troops moving away from Bab el-Mandeb? The Southern Armed Forces said the repositioning is intended to secure the southern city of Aden, "and the neighboring governorates, as well as strengthening the frontlines and addressing existing threats." Aden, which has a population of over a million people, is the interim seat of the Yemeni government, formally known as the Presidential Leadership Council (PLC). The Southern Armed Forces also intend to end the Houthi siege over the strategic southwestern city of Taiz. Nearly two million people live in Taiz, Yemen's third-largest city. The siege is raising fears of famine for residents, as well as a possible medical crisis as hospitals face restricted supplies. Houthis advancing towards Aden The Houthis control much of northwest Yemen, including the capital Sanaa. The rebels are a Shiite militant group backed by Iran. The US, Canada and several other countries regard them as a terror organization. The Houthis in September launched a rapid offensive against the PLC, seizing much of the coastline along the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean. It is also a key corridor for maritime trade and energy shipments. The Houthis have taken control of the major port town of Mocha in September, firming their grip over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The latest redeployment of the Southern Armed Forces is likely to give the rebels even more control over the strategic area. Sources told AFP news agency that Houthi forces are now just 60 kilometers (less than 40 miles) from Aden. The conflict between the Yemeni government and the Houthis has lasted for over 10 years. The fighting in Yemen, the poorest country in the Arab world, has been fueled by the wider rivalry between Iran and Saudi Arabia. In recent weeks, the Houthis have been launching frequent attacks on Saudi Arabia. On Sunday, the rebels claimed that they targeted the King Khalid International Airport and financial district of the Saudi capital, Riyadh. Saudi Arabia has not confirmed the alleged Houthi attack. Apart from the headline, no changes have been made in the report by ABP Live.

articles.title: Trump’s China trip faces complication after Nvidia CEO scandal
articles.description: WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump is preparing to depart for Asia on Monday, turning his focus to economic deals and historic three-way nuclear talks with Russia and China as his administration adjusts to a new political reality in Washington. Trump’s departure comes after the often-omnipresent president had remained largely out of public sight for the past several days, even as a nationwide ground stop snarled air traffic and the administration faced tough questions on its handling of the situation. His trip to Asia, which begins in Manila then continues to the Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen, gives Trump the opportunity to change the narrative from his domestic woes, including the air travel problems and fallout from the November midterm election where his party lost both chambers of Congress. The controversy over tech powerhouse and chipmaker Nvidia is also certain to hang over Trump’s visit to China, despite efforts by administration officials to downplay the president’s close ties to Jensen Huang, who resigned as CEO last week after admitting to an affair with an alleged Chinese government agent. Beijing has said it was not involved. Trump had no plans to raise the issue with Chinese President Xi Jinping when the two leaders meet, said U.S. officials who briefed reporters anonymously about the president’s Asia trip under ground rules set by the White House. Huang accompanied Trump on Air Force One during the president’s last trip to China in May, and he has been a sporadic presence around Trump at the White House while speaking to him frequently. Trump has argued that America needs to preserve its leadership on artificial intelligence, and warned of dire consequences if China wins that competition. Scrutiny of the Trump administration’s actions as they relate to Nvidia has been growing, including on the Commerce Department’s delay in placing restrictions on Nvidia chip exports to a company led by the alleged Chinese spy with whom Huang had the affair. Asked about the matter in an interview that aired Sunday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he will “leave the internal workings of the Commerce Department to the Commerce Department. “I think what’s more important here, Larry, is to examine whether Nvidia had a culture of compliance around the U.S. export restrictions ... and at what level?” Bessent told Fox News anchor Larry Kudlow. He added: “I think we’re going to see answers.” “Jensen Huang is an incredible innovator, but that does not abrogate their duties of compliance,” Bessent said. Among the travelers on the Asia trip with Trump will be Elon Musk, the head of SpaceX and Tesla, who is shaping up to be a top investigative target of the incoming Democratic majority in Congress. In the Philippines, Trump will meet with Southeast Asian leaders who look to the United States for help countering Beijing’s aggression in the region. He plans to sign a trade deal with Thailand while in Manila, the White House said. Then he heads to China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit — and at the end of the trip, the first-ever three-way talks with China's Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss nuclear stockpiles. Trump and U.S. officials have indicated that the meeting with Putin and Xi will focus on nuclear weapons and that topics of discussion would not include Russia's war in Ukraine, now in its fifth year. Still, the president has recently played up chances for a settlement to the conflict. The three-way meeting will also put in the spotlight the ongoing U.S. war with Iran, a country which has often allied with China and Russia. The war has been widely blamed for the Republican Party’s steep losses in the midterms, and while Trump has tried to play down the chances he will order a resumption of major strikes against Iran, he also has said he does not see the need for talks. China’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said Monday that the trilateral talks would be of “groundbreaking significance” and that China aimed to have in-depth exchanges about safeguarding world peace and promoting stability. “Under the current circumstances, the three countries shoulder an important responsibility to work together in addressing global challenges,” she said in a regular briefing in Beijing. This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/trump-asia-reset-deals-manila-050445131.html
